## Summary

Roll-up for initiative INIT-2026-11-18-ppa-v1: extract all formal and practical intelligence from Principles of Program Analysis into a vendor-neutral L0–L3 knowledge package with lossless issue tracking, deterministic validators, harness adapters and 11 adversarial gates. Child shards: ISS-W0-01, ISS-W0-02, ISS-W0-03, ISS-W1-01, ISS-W1-02, ISS-W2-01, ISS-W2-02, ISS-W2-03, ISS-W2-04, ISS-W3-01, ISS-W3-02, ISS-W4-01, ISS-W4-02, ISS-W5-01, ISS-W5-02, ISS-W5-03, ISS-W6-01, ISS-W6-02, ISS-W7-01, ISS-W8-01, ISS-W8-02.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- Whole book (book pp. 1–452; PDF pp. 21–465; 465 PDF pages)
- Coordinate source of truth: `corpus/pdf_page_map.json` (variable PDF offset; never assume a constant offset).

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Target altitudes: L0, L1, L2, L3. Altitudes per architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md §3.1: R0 always-on = 0 bytes; L0 = zero always-on bytes (router 50–99L and ambient 80–250L files loaded on match only); L1 = references (<=450L) with every side condition preserved; L2 = actionable skill procedures (250–499L) with explicit precondition checks; L3 = corpus shards and concept graph.

## Acceptance Gates

- [x] Artifact `MASTER_PLAN.md` exists and passes `scripts/validate_ppa_knowledge.py`
- [x] `python3 -B tests/test_wave0_foundation.py` and `python3 -B tests/test_artifact_rules.py` exit 0
- [x] `python3 -B scripts/check_portability_hygiene.py .` exits 0
- [x] `python3 -B scripts/issue_ctl.py validate` exits 0

## 3-Model Adversarial Alignment & Rebuttal Log

- 2026-11-19 Completed all `12/12` adversarial gates (`Gate #0` through `Gate #11`) with unanimous `3/3 [ALIGNED ...]` across `P-SWE`, `P-ARCH`, and `P-CYBER`, culminating in Gate #11 Round 2 unanimous `3/3 [ALIGNED gate11-v2]` (`#295`, `#296`, `#297`; `0 HARD_BLOCK`, `0 BLOCKING`, `0 PREFERENCE`), `21/21` child shards closed, `8/8` refactors closed (`REF-001..008`), `92/92` backlog items synced (`C6.6`–`C6.8`), `55/55` canonical & live port conformance checks passing, and live non-destructive deployment verified.

## Cross-Referenced Concepts & Artifacts

- Parent: none; depends on: none; blocks: none
- `MASTER_PLAN.md`
- `issues/shards/`

## Verification Receipts

- 2026-11-19 [closed] Closed all 12 gates (Gate #0-#11), 21/21 shards, 8/8 refactors, 92/92 backlog items, 5/5 adapters CONFORMANT 55/55, and live local deployments.

## Summary

Adding S → S leaves the inductive reading of Example B.2 unchanged but makes the coinductive reading all of {0,1,2}^∞; lfp and gfp coincide for the contractive functional 𝒬₀ but not for 𝒬₁–𝒬₃. Excluding strings containing 2 from the coinductive reading uses an inductive argument.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Example B.2, p. 415] (book p. 415; PDF p. 431)
- [PPA §B.2, p. 410] (book p. 410; PDF p. 426)
- [PPA Example B.2, p. 414] (book p. 414; PDF p. 430)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 0 extraction.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Checkers that accept a goal already on the visited stack implement gfp; an unguarded self-reference (A trusts A, type T = T) is then accepted, widening acceptance to everything (G-U0-25). By §B.2 (p. 410), requiring recursive calls to strictly decrease along a well-founded order (such as (ℕ, <) for 𝒬₀) collapses lfp = gfp (G-U0-21) — whereas on non-well-founded infinite strings {0,1,2}^∞ (Example B.2), productive constructor-guarded rules admit {0,1}^ω under gfp without collapsing to lfp. Conversely, assuming gfp-defined sets need only coinductive reasoning misses the inductive step of Example B.2.

Guardrail: L2: state whether a recursive specification uses lfp or gfp; reject unguarded trivial self-rules in coinductive checkers by requiring productive/constructor-guarded recursion `[external]` (whereas strictly decreasing recursion along a well-founded order forces lfp = gfp).

Table C.1 and the dominator definition assume a handle H from which every node is reachable; Example C.6 states that final(S) is a handle of the backward flow graph `(labels(S), flowᴿ(S))` for WHILE statements (which holds unconditionally by structural syntax because `final(while [b]^ℓ do S₀) = {ℓ}`).

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §C.1, p. 419] (book p. 419; PDF p. 434)
- [PPA §C.1, p. 420] (book p. 420; PDF p. 435)
- [PPA Table C.1, p. 421] (book p. 421; PDF p. 436)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 0 extraction (G-U0-30, G-U0-31).

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

In WHILE, `flow(S)` and `final(S)` are purely syntactic, so even semantically non-terminating loops (`while [true]^1 do [skip]^2`) remain syntactically reachable from `final(S)` in `flowᴿ(S)`. By contrast, in general compiler/binary CFGs `[external]`, dead blocks or undiscovered indirect-jump targets are unreachable from the entry (so DFS leaves them unnumbered and greatest-solution dominator equations give them `Dom(n) = N`), and syntactic exit-less sink loops (e.g. `for(;;)` with no `break`/`return` edge) leave loop nodes unreachable from exit blocks in the backward CFG, invalidating naive post-dominance claims (`[external]`).

Guardrail: L2: verify the handle covers every node (add a dummy root for multiple entries); track unreachable components explicitly instead of letting them inherit ⊤.

## Summary

Back edges and d(G, T) are defined relative to a DFSF T; Lemma C.12 makes them coincide with dominator-back edges only for reducible graphs; Example C.13 equates d(G) with the maximum loop nesting depth for uniquely labelled WHILE statements.

## Source Citations & Grounding

For Figure C.3, which of the two edges between n₁ and n₂ is a back edge depends on T (though symmetric Figure C.3 happens to have d(G, T) = 1 under both DFSFs, larger irreducible multi-entry graphs have T-dependent d(G, T)). ## Summary

Live Variables analysis may be used as the basis for Dead Code Elimination: an assignment to a variable that is not live at the exit from its label can be eliminated [PPA §2.1, p. 49] (book p. 49; PDF p. 68). The analysis is defined in Table 2.4 with no variables live at the end of the program; the book itself cautions on the same page that "for some applications it might be better to assume that all variables are live at the end of the program". Faint-variable analysis (Chapter 2 Exercises) strengthens the licence.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Table 2.4, p. 50] (book p. 50; PDF p. 69)

[external] Zeroing a key buffer before return is exactly such a dead store; an optimiser applying the analysis removes it and leaves secrets in memory.

## Summary

Printed signatures declare ud, du, UD, DU over Lab⋆ even though ud(z, 3) = {?} returns '?' and du(z, ?) = {3} branches on '?'.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §2.1.5, p. 53] (book p. 53; PDF p. 72)
- [PPA Example 2.12, p. 53] (book p. 53; PDF p. 72)
- [PPA §2.1.5, p. 54] (book p. 54; PDF p. 73)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 2 extraction.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

When an execution reads a variable `x` before any intervening assignment reaches that label, `RD_entry(ℓ')` contains `(x, ?)`. Under `Example 2.12` (`[z=x]^3` with uninitialised `z`), `UD(z, 3) = {?}` and `DU(z, ?) = {3}`. Typing these maps strictly as `Var⋆ × Lab⋆ → 𝒫(Lab⋆)` excludes `?` from valid indices, dropping uninitialised-use edges or failing domain assertions (`? ∉ Lab⋆`, `BKL-035`) inside `Mini Project 2.1` constant-folding checks (`? ∈ UD(x, ℓ')` must block rewriting).

Guardrail: Type all ud/du/UD/DU APIs cleanly with Lab⋆^? = Lab⋆ ∪ {?} in domain/codomain. (Refs: F-U2a-05, G-U2a-14, BKL-035).

## Summary

LV^⊆ on p. 60 suppresses flow^R edges at final(S⋆) without stating isolated exits, causing trailing while-loops and [seq₁]/[seq₂] sub-statements to violate Lemma 2.18 and Theorem 2.21.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §2.2.2, p. 60] (book p. 60; PDF p. 79)
- [PPA Lemma 2.18, p. 61] (book p. 61; PDF p. 80)
- [PPA Theorem 2.21, p. 64] (book p. 64; PDF p. 83)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 2 extraction.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Because `p. 60` defines `LV_exit(ℓ) ⊇ ∅` whenever `ℓ ∈ final(S⋆)` (using `⋃{LV_entry(ℓ') | (ℓ', ℓ) ∈ flow^R(S⋆)}` only `otherwise`), any program ending in a loop—such as `S = while [x>0]^1 do [x:=x-y]^2` where `final(S) = {1}` and `(1, 2) ∈ flow(S)`—gives `live_exit(1) = ∅ ⊉ {x, y} = live_entry(2)`. This yields a concrete counterexample to `Lemma 2.18` and breaks `Theorem 2.21(i)` under step `[wh₁]` (`σ₁ = {x↦1, y↦0}` and `σ₂ = {x↦1, y↦5}` satisfy `σ₁ ∼_{N(1)} σ₂`, then diverge on `N(2) = {x, y}`), as well as `[seq₁]`/`[seq₂]` sub-statements whose internal `while` bodies lack isolated exits even when the outer `S⋆` has isolated exits.

Guardrail: Always formulate constraints unconditionally as LV_exit(ℓ) ⊇ ⋃{...} ⊔ ι^ℓ_E (§2.3) in both solvers and proofs. (Refs: F-U2a-09, G-U2a-18, G-U2a-19).

## Summary

Example 2.30 states h <= v*b overlooking the v initial pairs (x, ?) (so h <= v*(b+1)), and label consistency gives h <= b+v -> O(b^2) when v = O(b).

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Example 2.30, p. 78] (book p. 78; PDF p. 97)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 2 extraction.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Each variable `x ∈ Var⋆` can carry its uninitialised reaching pair `(x, ?)` alongside labelled definitions `(x, ℓ)` (`|Lab⋆^?| = b + 1`), so the full height of `(𝒫(Var⋆ × Lab⋆^?), ⊆)` is `h ≤ v · (b + 1)` rather than `v · b`. Even under label consistency (where each label `ℓ` maps to at most one assigned variable `x`, giving `b` labelled pairs), there remain up to `v` distinct uninitialised pairs `(x, ?)`, yielding `h ≤ b + v` and total worklist complexity `O(e · (b + v)) = O(b · (b + v))`; `O(b²)` holds only under the hidden regularity assumption `v = O(b)`.

Guardrail: Include (x, ?) in lattice height accounting and state v = O(b) side condition when quoting O(b^2). (Refs: F-U2a-14, G-U2a-31).

## Summary

§2.5 embellishes a monotone framework, yet the book itself flags an important snag: the call and return transfer functions for large assumption sets are in general not monotone.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §2.5, p. 100] (book p. 100; PDF p. 119)
- [PPA Lemma 2.29, p. 75] (book p. 75; PDF p. 94)
- [PPA §2.4, p. 76] (book p. 76; PDF p. 95)
- [PPA §2.4, p. 77] (book p. 77; PDF p. 96)
- [PPA Chapter 2 Concluding Remarks, p. 129] (book p. 129; PDF p. 148)
- Coordinates validated against `corpus/pdf_page_map.json`; formulas must be confirmed against the rendered page image (see BKL-011).

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Adding a fact at a call site replaces the exact context key instead of extending it, so f(Z1) ⊑ f(Z2) can fail for Z1 ⊑ Z2 (derived from the definitions on p. 100). Termination of the worklist algorithm is not lost: the termination part of the proof of Lemma 2.29 uses only that each update joins into a strictly larger value and that the lattice satisfies the Ascending Chain Condition [PPA Lemma 2.29, p. 75] (book p. 75; PDF p. 94), [PPA §2.4, p. 76] (book p. 76; PDF p. 95). What is lost is the guarantee that the result is the least (MFP) solution: the correctness part of the proof uses the monotonicity of the transfer functions [PPA §2.4, p. 77] (book p. 77; PDF p. 96).

Guardrail: L2: treat the snag as a precision and least-solution issue, not a non-termination issue, and pick one of the book's remedies: (1) solving techniques for weakly monotonic systems of equations, referenced in the Concluding Remarks [PPA Chapter 2 Concluding Remarks, p. 129] (book p. 129; PDF p. 148); (2) the more approximate, monotone definition that relaxes the equality on the context component to an inclusion; (3) small assumption sets [PPA §2.5, p. 100] (book p. 100; PDF p. 119). Never feed exact large-assumption-set context keys into a monotone solver without stating the snag.

## Summary

§2.5 instantiates backward interprocedural analysis with F = flow⋆^R, E = final⋆, IF = inter-flow⋆^R without defining ^R on semicolon flows or 4-tuples.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §2.5, p. 85] (book p. 85; PDF p. 104)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 2 extraction.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Forward `§2.5` distinguishes semicolon interprocedural call/return arcs `(ℓ_c; ℓ_n)` and `(ℓ_x; ℓ_r)` in `flow⋆` from matched 4-tuples `(ℓ_c, ℓ_n, ℓ_x, ℓ_r)` in `inter-flow⋆`. Page 85 notes briefly that backward analyses take `F = flow⋆^R`, `E = final⋆`, and `IF = inter-flow⋆^R` without spelling out the reversal rules: orienting semicolon arcs backwards gives `(ℓ_n; ℓ_c)` and `(ℓ_r; ℓ_x)`, while reversing 4-tuples flips both control endpoints and entry/exit roles to `(ℓ_r, ℓ_x, ℓ_n, ℓ_c)` so post-call liveness propagates backward through callee exit `ℓ_x` to call entry `ℓ_c` while restoring pre-return caller facts via `f̂²`.

Guardrail: Define semicolon reversal (ℓ_n; ℓ_c), (ℓ_r; ℓ_x) and 4-tuple orientation (ℓ_r, ℓ_x, ℓ_n, ℓ_c) explicitly for backward passes. (Refs: F-U2b-01, G-U2b-03).

## Summary

With L=𝒫(D), ι ⊆ D so printed ι̂ = {({ι}, ι)} and {(ι, ι)} are ill-typed unless ι is identified with a single d₀; Example 2.41 drops braces and formals u, v and varies y instead of u.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §2.5.5, p. 99] (book p. 99; PDF p. 118)
- [PPA Example 2.41, p. 99] (book p. 99; PDF p. 118)
- [PPA §2.5.5, p. 100] (book p. 100; PDF p. 119)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 2 extraction.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

For `L = 𝒫(D)` in `§2.5.5`, the extremal element `ι` is already a subset `ι ⊆ D`. Writing `ι̂ = {({ι}, ι)}` (Large) and `{(ι, ι)}` (Small) commits a set-level type mismatch whenever `|ι| ≠ 1`, because `Δ = 𝒫(D)` expects `(δ ∈ 𝒫(D), d ∈ D)` pairs and `Δ = D` expects `(d₁ ∈ D, d₂ ∈ D)` pairs. Additionally, `Example 2.41` writes 3-component state tuples (`(u, a, ...)` without formal parameters `(x, y)` on Fibonacci's 5-variable store) and varies `y` instead of `u`, obscuring the non-monotonicity witness (`Z₁ = {(δ₀, d₁)} ⊆ Z₂ = {(δ₀, d₁), (δ₀, d₂)}` shrinks `{d'' | (δ, d'') ∈ Z}` output tags).

Guardrail: Use well-typed {(ι, d) | d ∈ ι} (large) and {(d, d) | d ∈ ι} (small), plus monotone ⊆ or small assumption sets (BKL-003). (Refs: F-U2b-06, G-U2b-12, G-U2b-13, BKL-003).

## Summary

IAV(p) = (AV(S) \ {x}) ∪ ... subtracts val formal x but forgets res formal y (leaking callee res writes as global mutations, masked in Example 2.42), and pp. 102-103 write 'context-insensitive' for flow-insensitive.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §2.5.6, p. 102] (book p. 102; PDF p. 121)
- [PPA §2.5.6, p. 103] (book p. 103; PDF p. 122)
- [PPA Example 2.42, p. 103] (book p. 103; PDF p. 122)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 2 extraction.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Under `§2.5.6`, `IAV(p)` should exclude parameters/locals scoped strictly inside `p`'s stack frame so only globally visible modifications propagate across `CP(S)`. Omitting `res y` from `AV(S) \ {x}` causes every write to out-parameter `y` inside `p` to remain in `IAV(p)` and falsely taint callers across the call graph (masked in `Example 2.42` only because `fib` and `add` carry no `res` parameter); meanwhile `pp. 102–103` twice misname flow-insensitive summaries as "context-insensitive". Solving `IAV` for `gfp` degenerates to `Var⋆` on self-recursive cycles (`fib`).

## Summary

℘, 𝒜, ℬ are defined on infinitely many (σ, ℋ) ∈ State × Heap yet write →_fin ('partial function with finite domain') instead of plain partial arrow ⇀.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §2.6.1, p. 107] (book p. 107; PDF p. 126)

Concrete semantic maps `℘ : (PExp × State × Heap) →_fin (Z + Loc + {◇})`, `𝒜`, and `ℬ` range over curried pairs `(σ, ℋ)` from `State × Heap`, which is infinite (`State = Var⋆ → (Z + Loc + {◇})` and unbounded `Loc`). VIII]`) is ill-typed and must be read as ordinary partial functions `⇀`.

## Summary

℘, 𝒜, ℬ are defined on infinitely many (σ, ℋ) ∈ State × Heap yet write →_fin ('partial function with finite domain') instead of plain partial arrow ⇀.

## Source Citations & Grounding

## Summary

Boolean guards [not is-nil(x)] act as identity, Case 1 maps nil-deref in [x:=y.sel] to {kill_x(...)} without raising a fault, and absent GC inflates 𝒫(SG) past 50 graphs on 7-block list reversal.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §2.6.3, p. 116] (book p. 116; PDF p. 135)
- [PPA §2.6.3, p. 120] (book p. 120; PDF p. 139)
- [PPA Exercise 2.21, p. 139] (book p. 139; PDF p. 158)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 2 extraction.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Three operational pitfalls limit naive `§2.6` implementations: (1) Boolean tests such as `[not is-nil(x)]` act as identity transfers, failing to prune null branches; (2) `[x := y.sel]` Case 1 silently maps null/missing-selector dereferences to `{kill_x(...)}` rather than aborting or emitting a fault, allowing post-crash paths to survive; (3) Neither `kill_x` nor `kill_{x.sel}` removes unreachable nodes from `n_∅`, pushing simple 7-block list reversal (`Exercise* 2.21`) above 50 abstract shape graphs unless GC, allocation-site naming (`n_{ℓ,X}`), or single-summary merging is introduced.

Guardrail: Emit client null-deref diagnostics from Shape∘(ℓ) before Case 1 transfer, pair with [b]^{ℓ₁,ℓ₂} branch splits, and adopt GC / n_{ℓ,X} / single-summary merging [148, 149]. (Refs: G-U2b-17, G-U2b-23, G-U2b-24, G-U2b-28).

## Summary

Page 142 uses semicolon multi-let sugar absent from the single-binding FUN grammar; pp. 146 and 155 have minor prose typos; Table 3.2 [app_fun] appends [x |-> v_2] rightmost after [f |-> close ...]; Table 3.3 [let_2] restricts to FV(e_2) without subtracting x.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §3.1, p. 142] (book p. 142; PDF p. 160)
- [PPA §3.1.1, p. 146] (book p. 146; PDF p. 164)
- [PPA Table 3.2, p. 155] (book p. 155; PDF p. 173)
- [PPA Table 3.3, p. 156] (book p. 156; PDF p. 174)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 3 extraction and Gate #5 audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Formal FUN grammar (`t ::= let x = e1 in e2`) permits one binding per `let`, so semicolon chains on p. 142 require nested desugaring. In Table 3.2 `[app_fun]`, `rho2 = rho1[f |-> close (fun f x => e1) in rho1]` and `(bind rho2[x |-> v2] in e1)^l` places `[x |-> v2]` rightmost (matching Example 3.8 `[f |-> ...][x |-> ...]`). In Table 3.3 `[let_2]`, `rho0 = rho | FV(e2)` omits subtracting `x`, retaining shadowed outer `x` underneath `[x |-> v]`.

Guardrail: Desugar multi-binding let into nested AST nodes, keep [x |-> v_2] rightmost in [app_fun], and read [let_2] rho_0 = rho | FV(e_2) verbatim. (Refs: F-U3a-01..04, G-U3a-01, G-U3a-02, G-U3a-08, G-U3a-09, G-U3a-11).

## Summary

Table 3.7 counts O(n^3) edge traversals assuming unit-cost add(p_2, D[p_1]) (which costs O(n^4) elementary operations under naive whole-set scans), requires dual registration in E[p_1] and E[p], and computes the least solution of |=_s / C_*[[e_*]] rather than minimal |= on dead closures.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §3.3, p. 168] (book p. 168; PDF p. 186)
- [PPA Table 3.7, p. 178] (book p. 178; PDF p. 196)
- [PPA §3.4.2, p. 181] (book p. 181; PDF p. 199)
- [PPA Corollary 3.25, p. 182] (book p. 182; PDF p. 200)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 3 extraction.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

A literal translation of Table 3.7 runs in `O(n^4)` scalar operations whenever `add(p_2, D[p_1])` scans entire closure sets instead of enqueueing individual `(q, t)` pairs with bitsets. Omitting conditional registration from either `E[p_1]` or `E[p]` makes the worklist order-sensitive and drops return/argument flows when `D[p_1]` arrives before `{t} <= D[p]`. Finally, Corollary 3.25 proves soundness `|=` rather than minimality because dead lambda bodies still seed `C_*(l)` under `|=_s`.

Guardrail: Register conditionals in both E[p_1] and E[p], propagate differential (q, t) pairs with O(1) bitset lookups [external], and gate dead lambdas via Mini Project 3.1 R_hat or lazy [9] expansion when needed. (Refs: G-U3a-17, G-U3a-19, G-U3a-24, G-U3a-25, G-U3a-26).

## Summary

Uniform k-CFA has exponential worst-case complexity for positive k; the book separately discusses a polynomial variant and the Cartesian Product Algorithm.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Table 3.10, p. 192] (book p. 192; PDF p. 210)
- [PPA §3.6, p. 195] (book p. 195; PDF p. 213)
- [PPA §3.6, p. 196] (book p. 196; PDF p. 214)
- Coordinates validated against `corpus/pdf_page_map.json`; formulas must be confirmed against the rendered page image (see BKL-011).

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

The book relates the interprocedural analysis of §2.5 (call strings) and uniform k-CFA: their abstract caches "have the same overall functionality" and "the two analyses are variations over a theme" [PPA §3.6, p. 196] (book p. 196; PDF p. 214). The book does not compare their costs. [external] In practice the cost of call-string context differs between first-order data flow and higher-order control flow analysis; summaries that present k-CFA as a cheap refinement smooth away the exponential worst-case bound the book states for uniform k-CFA with k > 0.

Guardrail: L1 comparison entry must carry the bound with its parameters; L2 chooses the context abstraction per language paradigm.

## Acceptance Gates

- [ ] Affected artifacts carry a one-line pointer to this item (non-blocking rule, `architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md` §6.4)

## Summary

On p. 197, printed CPA [app] omits a closing parenthesis ")" before ^l and writes {delta_b} <= rho_hat(x_1) x ... x rho_hat(x_m) omitting ", delta_b"; p. 198 writes Delta = Term; any empty argument C_hat(l_j, delta) = empty collapses the Cartesian product to empty.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §3.6.2, p. 196] (book p. 196; PDF p. 214)
- [PPA §3.6.2, p. 197] (book p. 197; PDF p. 215)
- [PPA §3.6.2, p. 198] (book p. 198; PDF p. 216)
- [PPA Exercise 3.17, p. 209] (book p. 209; PDF p. 227)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 3 extraction and Gate #5 audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

In §3.6.2 `CPA`, `Env_hat = (Var x Delta) -> Val_hat` takes two arguments `(x_i, delta_b)` as shown in `[var]` (`rho_hat(x, delta)`), so p. 197's `{delta_b} <= rho_hat(x_1) x ... x rho_hat(x_m)` omits `, delta_b` and drops `)` before `^l` in `(t_0^{l_0}(t_1^{l_1}, ..., t_m^{l_m})^l` (the body `t_b^{l_b}` and `C_hat(l_b, delta_b) <= C_hat(l, delta)` are printed cleanly). Separately, if any argument `j` evaluates solely to a base constant with empty `C_hat(l_j, delta) = empty`, the Cartesian product becomes empty and skips the call body.

Guardrail: Bind {delta_b} <= rho_hat(x_1, delta_b) x ... x rho_hat(x_m, delta_b), read p. 198 Delta as union_{m>=1} Term^m, and populate base-type tokens in C_hat(l_j, delta) so non-function arguments do not empty the product. (Refs: F-U3b-05, F-U3b-06, G-U3b-17..20, BKL-007).

## Summary

Env_hat = Var -> Val_hat collapses shadowed bindings like dynamic scoping unless alpha-renamed; in Set Constraints (p. 201), S_1 intersect S_2 preserves monotonicity whereas complement ~S and variable-LHS guards (S_1 <= S_2) => S_3 break Tarski's Theorem; lazy solving ([9]) omits dead lambdas included by Table 3.6.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Chapter 3 Concluding Remarks, p. 199] (book p. 199; PDF p. 217)
- [PPA Chapter 3 Concluding Remarks, p. 201] (book p. 201; PDF p. 219)
- [PPA Chapter 3 Concluding Remarks, p. 202] (book p. 202; PDF p. 220)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 3 extraction and Gate #5 audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Because `0-CFA` `Env_hat = Var -> Val_hat` keys variables by raw name, two distinct functions or nested `let` blocks declaring `x` merge values unless `alpha`-renamed to unique identifiers. In Set-Constraint Based Analysis (p. 201), union `∪`, intersection `∩`, constructors `C(...)`, and projections `C^{-i}(S)` are monotone on `(P(U), <=)`, whereas explicit complement `¬S` (anti-monotone) and variable-LHS conditional guards `(S1 <= S2) => S3` violate monotonicity so Tarski's Fixed Point Theorem fails and Banach's Contraction Theorem is needed. Separately, `[9]`'s (`[external: Aiken et al.]`) lazy expansion skips unreachable closures eagerly seeded by `Table 3.6`.

Guardrail: Alpha-rename distinct variable bindings before 0-CFA, exclude ¬S / variable-LHS guards from monotone Tarski solvers, and distinguish lazy [9] reachability from whole-AST Table 3.6. (Refs: G-U3a-03, G-U3b-22, G-U3b-23, G-U3b-24).

## Summary

The book evaluates arithmetic over unbounded integers and states that no errors can occur (division by 0 must still produce an integer); the Interval lattice ranges over integers extended with infinities. [external] Machine arithmetic wraps modulo 2^w or is undefined on signed overflow; the book does not discuss machine arithmetic.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Table 2.5, p. 55] (book p. 55; PDF p. 74)
- [PPA §4.2, p. 221] (book p. 221; PDF p. 238)
- Coordinates validated against `corpus/pdf_page_map.json`; formulas must be confirmed against the rendered page image (see BKL-011).

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

[external] An Interval transfer function sound over the integers is unsound over 32/64-bit two's-complement values: [0, MAX] + [1, 1] is [1, MAX+1] mathematically but wraps negative at runtime, defeating upper-bound checks; folding that relies on signed-overflow UB can delete overflow guards.

Guardrail: L2 procedures that reuse Interval/Sign analyses on machine integers must state the wrap-around model (wrapped intervals [external]) or add explicit overflow proof obligations; division by zero is a fault sink.

## Summary

Upper bound operators (and hence widenings) are explicitly not required to be monotone, commutative, associative or absorptive.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §4.2, p. 225] (book p. 225; PDF p. 242)
- [PPA §4.2, p. 226] (book p. 226; PDF p. 243)
- [PPA Chapter 6 Exercises, p. 391] (book p. 391; PDF p. 407)
- Coordinates validated against `corpus/pdf_page_map.json`; formulas must be confirmed against the rendered page image (see BKL-011).

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

A widening operator is an upper bound operator [PPA §4.2, p. 226] (book p. 226; PDF p. 243), and upper bound operators are not required to be monotone [PPA §4.2, p. 225] (book p. 225; PDF p. 242). A summary that treats widening as monotone therefore states a property the book does not give: a larger input to ∇ need not give a larger result, and ∇ need not be commutative (the book's interval example on p. 225 gives different results for swapped arguments), so precision of the widened iteration can depend on the order in which values arrive. Exercise 6.13 asks for a worklist algorithm with widening and for proofs that it over-approximates the least solution and terminates even without the Ascending Chain Condition. Note that x ⊔ (x ∇ y) = x ∇ y, because x ∇ y ⊒ x for an upper bound operator; that wrapping is not a hazard.

Guardrail: L2: never claim that a widening operator is monotone, commutative, associative or absorptive; quote the termination argument for the widened iteration, not a monotonicity argument. [external] In chaotic-iteration solvers, apply widening only at cycle cut points (e.g. targets of back edges for a depth-first spanning forest) and follow with narrowing where precision matters.

## Summary

Book p. 230 remarks that narrowing Delta is not required to be absorptive (l Delta l = l), yet instantiating l_2 <= l_1 => l_2 <= (l_1 Delta l_2) <= l_1 at l_1 = l_2 = l forces l <= l Delta l <= l, so l Delta l = l always holds.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §4.2.2, p. 230] (book p. 230; PDF p. 247)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 4 extraction and Gate #6 audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Section 4.2.2 axiomatically requires l_2 <= l_1 => l_2 <= (l_1 Delta l_2) <= l_1 plus descending chain stabilisation, then asserts in prose (p. 230) that Delta need not be absorptive (l Delta l = l). Evaluating the contractiveness axiom at the reflexive pair l_1 = l_2 = l forces l <= (l Delta l) <= l and hence l Delta l = l by antisymmetry, which explains why ([f]_Delta^n)_n needs no reductive if-guard inside Red(f).

Guardrail: Treat every contractive narrowing operator as unconditionally absorptive on diagonal inputs (l Delta l = l) and enter narrowing strictly inside Red(f) (Refs: F-U4a-07, G-U4a-14).

## Summary

Example 4.15 special-cases only int_1 = int_2 = bot; for int_1 = bot and int_2 = [z_3, z_4], inf(bot) = inf > z_3 and sup(bot) = -inf < z_4 trigger LB_K(inf, z_3) and UB_K(-inf, z_4) (giving [-inf, inf] when K = empty).

## Summary

Example 4.15 special-cases only int_1 = int_2 = bot; for int_1 = bot and int_2 = [z_3, z_4], inf(bot) = inf > z_3 and sup(bot) = -inf < z_4 trigger LB_K(inf, z_3) and UB_K(-inf, z_4) (giving [-inf, inf] when K = empty).

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Example 4.15, p. 228] (book p. 228; PDF p. 245)
- [PPA Example 4.15, p. 229] (book p. 229; PDF p. 246)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 4 extraction and Gate #6 audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

On p. 229, Example 4.15's piecewise int_1 nabla_K int_2 formula filters out only the double-bottom pair int_1 = int_2 = bot before branching to [LB_K(inf(int_1), inf(int_2)), UB_K(sup(int_1), sup(int_2))]. Because Example 4.10 defines inf(bot) = inf and sup(bot) = -inf, step 1 with int_1 = bot and int_2 = [z_3, z_4] satisfies inf(bot) > z_3 and sup(bot) < z_4, immediately jumping to [-inf, inf] when K = empty.

Guardrail: Enforce bot nabla_K int_2 = int_2 and int_1 nabla_K bot = int_1 short-circuits in all interval widenings (cf. Exercise 4.6(4)) (Refs: F-U4a-05, G-U4a-13).

## Summary

On book p. 269, the 4th line of the '=>' derivation for Display (4.15) prints g(g_{nabla_L}^n) <= g_{nabla_M}^n, applying L-widening subscript nabla_L to g : M -> M instead of nabla_M.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Lemma 4.45, p. 269] (book p. 269; PDF p. 286)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 4 extraction and Gate #6 audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Inside Lemma 4.45's induction proof, abstract function g = alpha o f o gamma operates on M using iterates g_{nabla_M}^n, whereas nabla_L operates solely on L via f_{nabla_L}^n = gamma(g_{nabla_M}^n) in (4.14). Printing g(g_{nabla_L}^n) on line 4 of the '=>' derivation for (4.15) crosses carriers between L and M even though the next equality substitutes g_{nabla_M}^n and alpha o gamma <= id_M (4.9).

Guardrail: Read line 4 of the '=>' derivation for (4.15) as g(g_{nabla_M}^n) <= g_{nabla_M}^n and enforce gamma(bot_M) = bot_L whenever invoking Lemma 4.45 (Refs: F-U4b-06, G-U4b-17).

## Summary

Book p. 271 writes 'the construction of the reduced product [39] (see Section 4.3.)' and switches from rho[L] to rho_2(L), whereas reduced product is defined in Section 4.4.2 (p. 256).

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Chapter 4 Concluding Remarks, p. 271] (book p. 271; PDF p. 288)
- [PPA §4.4.2, p. 256] (book p. 256; PDF p. 273)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 4 extraction and Gate #6 audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Page 270 denotes the fixed-point image lattice of upper closure operator rho : L -> L with square brackets rho[L] = {rho(l) | l in L} = Fix(rho). Switching to round parentheses rho_2(L) subseteq rho_1(L) on p. 271 conflates lattice images with pointwise element application, and the parenthetical '(see Section 4.3.)' misdirects readers away from §4.4.2 (p. 256) where reduced products are formally constructed.

- [PPA Mini Project 4.3, p. 275] (book p. 275; PDF p. 292)

## Summary

Attaching transfer functions to labels forces f_ell^{SS}([b]^ell) = Sigma, propagating false-branch states into true-branches so SS strictly over-approximates collecting semantics; Constant Propagation p. 267 also leaves sigma_hat != bot tacit.

## Source Citations & Grounding

Node-attached Monotone Frameworks apply transfer functions per block before branching along F, forcing f_ell^{SS}([b]^ell) = Sigma = id (Remark p. 266) so false-branch states leak into true-branch targets and SS strictly over-approximates collecting semantics. ## Summary

Whereas gamma(alpha(l_1) nabla_M alpha(l_2)) induces a valid widening under Proposition 4.44, gamma(alpha(l_1) Delta_M alpha(l_2)) violates (l_1 Delta_L l_2) <= l_1 whenever l_1 notin gamma[M], even on finite Galois insertions.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Proposition 4.44, p. 268] (book p. 268; PDF p. 285)
- [PPA Exercise 4.24, p. 282] (book p. 282; PDF p. 299)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 4 extraction and Gate #6 audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Proposition 4.44 lifts widening via gamma(alpha(l_1) nabla_M alpha(l_2)) because extensiveness allows passing through the upward closure gamma(alpha(l_1)) >= l_1. By contrast, narrowing must satisfy (l_1 Delta_L l_2) <= l_1 whenever l_2 <= l_1; for any l_1 notin gamma[M], even a finite Galois insertion yields l_1 Delta_L l_1 = gamma(alpha(l_1)) > l_1, refuting contractiveness at the first reflexive pair.

Guardrail: Never induce narrowing via gamma(alpha(l_1) Delta_M alpha(l_2)); use descending truncators Upsilon in L (Exercise 4.11) or clamp with l_1 glb_L (...) under explicit step caps [external] (Refs: G-U4b-18).

Non-termination is modelled by the absence of a derivation in the natural semantics, so the subject-reduction style correctness result is vacuous for diverging programs.

## Source Citations & Grounding

## Summary

Table 5.5's if-clause returns (theta_4(theta_3 tau_2), theta_4 o theta_3 o theta_2 o theta_1), omitting o theta_0; on Gamma = [b |-> 'a] and if (b < 5) then 1 else 2, theta_0 = ['a |-> int] is dropped, allowing ill-typed ground instantiations.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Table 5.5, p. 303] (book p. 303; PDF p. 320)
- [PPA Table 5.8, p. 310] (book p. 310; PDF p. 327)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 5 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

In Table 5.5 [PPA Table 5.5, p. 303] (book p. 303; PDF p. 320), step 1 computes (tau_0, theta_0) = W_UL(Gamma, e_0) and threads theta_0 Gamma into e_1, but the final return tuple (theta_4(theta_3 tau_2), theta_4 o theta_3 o theta_2 o theta_1) drops o theta_0. On Gamma = [b |-> 'a] and e = if (b < 5) then 1 else 2, e_0 forces theta_0 = ['a |-> int], while theta_1..theta_4 are all id; returning theta = id leaves 'a unconstrained in theta Gamma, breaking Theorem 5.20 syntactic soundness because ground instantiation ['a |-> bool] produces an ill-typed guard (bool < 5). Table 5.8 [PPA Table 5.8, p. 310] (book p. 310; PDF p. 327) restores o theta_0.

Guardrail: Compose the full chain theta_4 o theta_3 o theta_2 o theta_1 o theta_0 as corrected in Table 5.8. (Refs: F-U5a-04, G-U5a-14).

## Summary

Section 5.3.4 defines dom(theta_A) = AV(C) (undefined otherwise), which fails to cover unconstrained annotation variables in (AV(theta Gamma_hat) union AV(tau_hat)) \ AV(C) such as '1 in fn_X x => x 1.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Corollary 5.23, p. 318] (book p. 318; PDF p. 335)
- [PPA §5.3.4, p. 319] (book p. 319; PDF p. 336)
- [PPA Mini Project 5.3, p. 355] (book p. 355; PDF p. 372)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 5 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Section 5.3.4 [PPA §5.3.4, p. 319] (book p. 319; PDF p. 336) defines the minimal annotation substitution theta_A(beta) = {pi | (beta >= {pi}) in C} on dom(theta_A) = AV(C) and 'undefined otherwise'. However, Corollary 5.23 [PPA Corollary 5.23, p. 318] (book p. 318; PDF p. 335) requires theta_G = theta_A o theta_T to be a ground substitution covering every annotation variable in AV(theta Gamma_hat) union AV(tau_hat). On fn_X x => x 1 (or Mini Project 5.3 [PPA Mini Project 5.3, p. 355] (book p. 355; PDF p. 372)), the parameter arrow carries a fresh annotation variable '1 appearing in tau_hat but absent from C, so applying theta_A leaves '1 ungrounded unless unconstrained variables default to empty.

Guardrail: Default theta_A(beta) = empty for all beta in (AV(theta Gamma_hat) union AV(tau_hat)) \ AV(C) when constructing covering ground validations. (Refs: F-U5a-08, F-U5b-01, G-U5a-19, G-U5a-21, G-U5b-01).

## Summary

Sections 5.1-5.3 require |-_UL typability (rejecting fn x => x x), assume base-only Const/Op and monomorphic let, discard internal call arrows from root types, smear monomorphic arguments bidirectionally, and rely on closed big-step evaluation.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §5.1, p. 283] (book p. 283; PDF p. 300)
- [PPA Table 5.1, p. 285] (book p. 285; PDF p. 302)
- [PPA Table 5.2, p. 288] (book p. 288; PDF p. 305)
- [PPA Example 5.4, p. 289] (book p. 289; PDF p. 306)
- [PPA Fact 5.6, p. 291] (book p. 291; PDF p. 308)
- [PPA Table 5.4, p. 292] (book p. 292; PDF p. 309)
- [PPA Theorem 5.9, p. 295] (book p. 295; PDF p. 312)
- [PPA Exercise 5.4, p. 359] (book p. 359; PDF p. 376)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 5 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Four structural gates constrain §§5.1-5.3: (1) Fact 5.6 [PPA Fact 5.6, p. 291] (book p. 291; PDF p. 308) ties |-_CFA to Table 5.1 |-_UL [PPA Table 5.1, p. 285] (book p. 285; PDF p. 302), so Robinson's occurs check rejects untyped self-application (fn x => x x) before analysis begins; (2) Table 5.2 [app] [PPA Table 5.2, p. 288] (book p. 288; PDF p. 305) drops the operator's arrow annotation from the conclusion, requiring the full derivation tree (Example 5.4 [PPA Example 5.4, p. 289] (book p. 289; PDF p. 306) and Exercise 5.4 display (5.2) [PPA Exercise 5.4, p. 359] (book p. 359; PDF p. 376)) to recover per-label C_hat(l); (3) monomorphic [let] and equality on [app] domain types smear argument annotations across distinct call sites; and (4) big-step Table 5.4 [PPA Table 5.4, p. 292] (book p. 292; PDF p. 309) lacks finite trees for diverging loops, making Theorem 5.9 [PPA Theorem 5.9, p. 295] (book p. 295; PDF p. 312) vacuous on non-terminating servers.

Guardrail: Enforce TYPED_SUBSTRATE_GATE, persist per-node AST type side tables ((5.2)), upgrade to §5.4 subtyping/polymorphism to eliminate smearing, and pair reactive loops with small-step SOS. (Refs: G-U5a-01, G-U5a-02, G-U5a-03, G-U5a-04, G-U5a-05, G-U5a-06, G-U5a-07, G-U5a-08, G-U5a-09, G-U5a-10, G-U5a-11, BKL-004).

## Summary

Syntactic Ann needs finite Pnt_* or P(Pnt) for completeness, and replacing §5.2.3's covariant domain precision order with §5.4's contravariant subtyping order breaks Proposition 5.12's Moore family on fn_X x => x.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §5.2.3, p. 298] (book p. 298; PDF p. 315)
- [PPA Proposition 5.12, p. 299] (book p. 299; PDF p. 316)
- [PPA §5.4.1, p. 324] (book p. 324; PDF p. 341)
- [PPA Exercise 5.9, p. 361] (book p. 361; PDF p. 378)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 5 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Proposition 5.12 [PPA Proposition 5.12, p. 299] (book p. 299; PDF p. 316) proves JUDG_CFA[Gamma |-_UL e : tau] is a Moore family under the pointwise covariant order <=_cov on Type_hat[tau] [PPA §5.2.3, p. 298] (book p. 298; PDF p. 315) (requiring finite Pnt_* or P(Pnt) so arbitrary meets exist). When a solver instead orders function types by §5.4.1's behavioral subtyping <= [PPA §5.4.1, p. 324] (book p. 324; PDF p. 341) (contravariant in domains, covariant in codomains), Exercise 5.9 [PPA Exercise 5.9, p. 361] (book p. 361; PDF p. 378) shows that two valid typings of fn_X x => x with different domain annotations have greatest lower bound (tau_1 u tau_2) --{X}--> (tau_1 n tau_2), whose codomain no longer accepts its widened argument, violating Moore-family closure and preventing a single unconstrained least typing.

Guardrail: Keep precision order <=_cov and behavioral subtyping <= distinct; use constrained type schemes when combining subtyping with polymorphism. (Refs: G-U5a-12, G-U5a-13, G-U5b-07).

Transcribing §§5.1-5.3 mechanically without checking each printed slip triggers concrete bugs: (1) Table 5.6 [PPA Table 5.6, p. 305] (book p. 305; PDF p. 322) emits self-binding [alpha |-> alpha] (and Table 5.7 [beta |-> beta]), which creates a self-cycle in naive [external: union-find] find() loops unless short-circuited to id; (2) Table 5.8's unhatted tau_1 [PPA Table 5.8, p. 310] (book p. 310; PDF p. 327) and §5.1.2/§5.2.2 missing turnstile subscripts [PPA §5.1.2, p. 290] (book p. 290; PDF p. 307) [PPA §5.2.2, p. 295] (book p. 295; PDF p. 312) conflate underlying Type with annotated Type_hat; (3) §5.3.1 p. 302 cites [fn] where Table 5.1 [fun] applies [PPA §5.3.1, p. 302] (book p. 302; PDF p. 319); and (4) reversed [beta' |-> beta] in Example 5.19 [PPA Example 5.19, p. 311] (book p. 311; PDF p. 328) and unprimed/unhatted binders in §5.3.2 p. 307 [PPA §5.3.2, p. 307] (book p. 307; PDF p. 324) and Theorem 5.21 pp. 315-316 [PPA Theorem 5.21, p. 315] (book p. 315; PDF p. 332) [PPA Theorem 5.21, p. 316] (book p. 316; PDF p. 333) cause regression test mismatches if compared by raw variable names instead of alpha-renaming.

issues.body:
## Summary

Exception analysis subtracts handled exceptions from effects (rule [handle], Table 5.10). On an effect variable the book defines β\{s} = β, even though β might later be instantiated to {s} [PPA §5.4, p. 329] (book p. 329; PDF p. 346). Generalisation must not quantify variables free in the effect (illustrated by Example 5.36).

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Table 5.10, p. 328] (book p. 328; PDF p. 345)
- [PPA §5.4, p. 329] (book p. 329; PDF p. 346)
- [PPA §5.4, p. 330] (book p. 330; PDF p. 347)
- [PPA Example 5.36, p. 346] (book p. 346; PDF p. 363)
- Coordinates validated against `corpus/pdf_page_map.json`; formulas must be confirmed against the rendered page image (see BKL-011).

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Per the book, β\{s} = β is semantically sound, because β\{s} ⊆ β should hold for all instantiations of β (as in rule [sub]); "to define a less approximate system" it would be natural to add φ ::= ··· | φ\{s} and extend the UCAI axiomatisation to set difference [PPA §5.4, p. 330] (book p. 330; PDF p. 347). Erasing the subtraction on effect variables is therefore sound but less precise; keeping φ\{s} symbolically is the more precise option. [external] Dropping the generalisation side condition admits type confusion through polymorphic channels and references.

Guardrail: L2: enforce the generalisation side condition explicitly; accept β\{s} = β as the sound default, and where precision matters represent subtraction on effect variables symbolically (φ\{s}) with the extended axiomatisation.

## Acceptance Gates

## Summary

Surface §5.4.1 syntax omits dynamic locations xi in Loc produced by new_pi's substitution e_2[x |-> xi], varpi's BNF omits braces around pi, and p. 323 prose calls operator e_1 'the argument e_1'.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §5.4.1, p. 319] (book p. 319; PDF p. 336)
- [PPA §5.4.1, p. 320] (book p. 320; PDF p. 337)
- [PPA §5.4.1, p. 321] (book p. 321; PDF p. 338)
- [PPA Table 5.9, p. 322] (book p. 322; PDF p. 339)
- [PPA §5.4.1, p. 323] (book p. 323; PDF p. 340)
- [PPA §5.4.1, p. 324] (book p. 324; PDF p. 341)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 5 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

In §5.4.1 [PPA §5.4.1, p. 319] (book p. 319; PDF p. 336) [PPA §5.4.1, p. 320] (book p. 320; PDF p. 337), evaluating new_pi x := e_1 in e_2 substitutes a fresh heap address xi in Loc into e_2[x |-> xi], producing runtime terms !xi and xi := e_0 that are ill-formed under the surface grammar restricting dereference/assignment to variables x; a mechanised Subject Reduction proof stalls unless intermediate syntax adds xi in Loc and a store-typing context. Separately, writing unbraced varpi ::= pi | varpi_1 u varpi_2 | empty [PPA §5.4.1, p. 321] (book p. 321; PDF p. 338) conflates singleton elements with sets, misreading p. 323's 'argument e_1' slip [PPA §5.4.1, p. 323] (book p. 323; PDF p. 340) swaps operator and operand roles in Table 5.9 [app] [PPA Table 5.9, p. 322] (book p. 322; PDF p. 339), and relaxing §5.4.1 p. 324 ref_varpi payload invariance [PPA §5.4.1, p. 324] (book p. 324; PDF p. 341) allows writing a subtype-incompatible closure through an aliased reference.

Guardrail: Extend intermediate runtime expressions with xi in Loc, normalise varpi to braced sets, enforce ref_varpi payload invariance, and keep {new pi} unmasked. (Refs: F-U5b-02, F-U5b-03, G-U5b-02, G-U5b-03, G-U5b-04, G-U5b-05, G-U5b-06, BKL-026, BKL-031).

## Summary

Table 5.11 [region] prints dom(sigma) for dom(sigma_1), Table 5.12 [var] prints sigma_hat for sigma_hat @ r, Table 5.13 [sub] invokes unstated Type_RI subtyping, and [region] requires both Observe and rho_vec in phi.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Table 5.11, p. 334] (book p. 334; PDF p. 351)
- [PPA Table 5.12, p. 337] (book p. 337; PDF p. 354)
- [PPA Table 5.13, p. 338] (book p. 338; PDF p. 355)
- [PPA §5.4.3, p. 339] (book p. 339; PDF p. 356)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 5 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

In Table 5.11 [region] [PPA Table 5.11, p. 334] (book p. 334; PDF p. 351), writing {rn_vec} intersect dom(sigma) = empty instead of dom(sigma_1) allows fresh regions to collide with allocations made during intermediate evaluation if store state sigma_1 already allocated rn_i, corrupting stack-region pop (sigma_2 \\ rn_vec) into dangling pointers. In Table 5.12 [var] [PPA Table 5.12, p. 337] (book p. 337; PDF p. 354), omitting '@ r' on sigma_hat conflates boxed extended types with unboxed schemes, while Table 5.13 [sub] [PPA Table 5.13, p. 338] (book p. 338; PDF p. 355) invokes <= without defining Type_RI variance (making r_1/r_2 covariant instead of invariant allows reading/writing across deallocated regions). Finally, applying [region] without BOTH Observe [PPA §5.4.3, p. 339] (book p. 339; PDF p. 356) and rho_vec occurring in phi wraps escaped return regions or inserts dead empty regions.

Guardrail: Check {rn_vec} intersect dom(sigma_1) = empty, keep r_1, r_2 invariant in Type_RI arrow subtyping, preserve compound forall[]. tau_hat, and verify rho_vec in phi before letregion wrapping. (Refs: F-U5b-05, F-U5b-06, F-U5b-07, G-U5b-13, G-U5b-14, G-U5b-15, G-U5b-16, G-U5b-17).

## Summary

Examples 5.35 and 5.37 write unbraced C for {C} (with an unmatched '(' in Example 5.35), and mutual Type_CA/Ann_CA recursion permits negative beta inside r?tau_hat or chan unless restricted to positive positions.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA §5.5.1, p. 344] (book p. 344; PDF p. 361)
- [PPA Example 5.35, p. 345] (book p. 345; PDF p. 362)
- [PPA Table 5.18, p. 348] (book p. 348; PDF p. 365)
- [PPA Example 5.37, p. 349] (book p. 349; PDF p. 366)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 5 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Three structural hazards govern §5.5.1 CML behaviours: (1) unbraced singleton C in Examples 5.35 and 5.37 [PPA Example 5.35, p. 345] (book p. 345; PDF p. 362) [PPA Example 5.37, p. 349] (book p. 349; PDF p. 366) violates Reg_CA set syntax [PPA §5.5.1, p. 344] (book p. 344; PDF p. 361) (and Example 5.35 prints an unmatched '('), breaking parsers enforcing set-typed regions {C}; (2) because Type_CA and Ann_CA are mutually recursive, allowing bound behaviour variable beta inside contravariant receive payloads (r?tau_hat) or invariant channels (tau_hat chan r) breaks monotonicity of rec beta.phi, invalidating coinductive Table 5.18 unfolding [PPA Table 5.18, p. 348] (book p. 348; PDF p. 365); and (3) adding left-distributivity phi_1 ; (phi_2 + phi_3) = (phi_1 ; phi_2) + (phi_1 ; phi_3) (intentionally omitted from Table 5.18) equates post-send branching with pre-send internal choice, masking synchronous [external: deadlocks].

Guardrail: Write braced singleton {C}, restrict rec beta.phi to strictly positive occurrences of beta, use coinductive [external: pair memoisation], and never apply left-distributivity. (Refs: F-U5b-08, F-U5b-09, F-U5b-10, G-U5b-18, G-U5b-19, G-U5b-20, G-U5b-21).

## Summary

Page 350 line 15 mis-cites Section 5.1 instead of Section 5.4 for shape-conformant subtyping, Mini Project 5.5 leaves 'undefined otherwise' implicit on base addition '+', and PDF OCR erases 21 rules/axioms plus display (5.2).

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Chapter 5 Concluding Remarks, p. 350] (book p. 350; PDF p. 367)
- [PPA Mini Project 5.4, p. 356] (book p. 356; PDF p. 373)
- [PPA Mini Project 5.5, p. 358] (book p. 358; PDF p. 375)
- [PPA Exercise 5.4, p. 359] (book p. 359; PDF p. 376)
- [PPA Exercise 5.13, p. 362] (book p. 362; PDF p. 379)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 5 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Summary

Uniquely labelled WHILE programs yield reducible graphs (Example C.13); Figure C.3 shows an irreducible graph. For instances of a Bit Vector Framework iterated in reverse postorder of a depth-first spanning forest T, the Round Robin bound of Lemma 6.12 (`d(G_S, T) + 3` iterations) is stated in terms of the loop connectedness parameter `d(G_S, T)`.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Lemma 6.12, p. 380] (book p. 380; PDF p. 396)
- [PPA Figure C.3, p. 425] (book p. 425; PDF p. 440)
- [PPA Lemma C.12, p. 425] (book p. 425; PDF p. 440)
- [PPA Example C.13, p. 425] (book p. 425; PDF p. 440)
- Coordinates validated against `corpus/pdf_page_map.json`; formulas must be confirmed against the rendered page image (see BKL-011).

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

[external] Binaries, goto-heavy C and obfuscated code produce irreducible graphs in which back edges depend on the spanning forest, natural-loop headers are ill-defined, and `d(G_S, T)` varies with the chosen DFSF `T`; moreover, non-bit-vector frameworks do not inherit Lemma 6.12's `d(G_S, T) + 3` cap.

Guardrail: L2: use strong components (§6.3) rather than structural reduction; quote `d(G_S, T) + 3` only for Bit Vector Framework instances with DFSF `T` and reverse postorder; [external] place widening at DFSF back-edge targets.

## Summary

Table 6.5 initialises scc := 1, shadows scc in 'for each scc in topological order do', writes srPostorder[x >= t] := (scc, rp), and increments scc := scc + 1.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Table 6.5, p. 382] (book p. 382; PDF p. 398)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 6 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Table 6.5 [PPA Table 6.5, p. 382] (book p. 382; PDF p. 398) initialises integer counter scc := 1, then rebinds the exact same identifier as the loop variable in 'for each scc in topological order do', computes local rPostorder on that component set, stores (scc, rp) into srPostorder[x >= t], and attempts scc := scc + 1. Under lexical scoping the inner set shadows the counter so every component receives a non-comparable set object or identical rank 1; under flat scoping the loop overwrites the integer with a set, raising a runtime type error on scc + 1 and breaking the lexicographic topological priority ordering required by Table 6.6.

Guardrail: Separate integer counter scc_id from component set comp in all derived pseudocode and implementations while preserving verbatim Table 6.5 at L3. (Refs: F-U6-08, G-U6-16).

## Summary

One-armed 'if c <= t_1 then t_2' terms omit an explicit false branch and require registering both guard and payload variables in infl; lazy online simplification also adds edges that can merge SCCs.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Example 6.2, p. 367] (book p. 367; PDF p. 383)
- [PPA Example 6.6, p. 373] (book p. 373; PDF p. 389)
- [PPA Mini Project 6.2, p. 388] (book p. 388; PDF p. 404)

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Example 6.2 [PPA Example 6.2, p. 367] (book p. 367; PDF p. 383) and Example 6.6 [PPA Example 6.6, p. 373] (book p. 373; PDF p. 389) encode Chapter 3 conditional implications as one-armed 'if c <= t_1 then t_2' terms without an explicit else-clause. If an evaluator leaves the false branch undefined or omits payload variables FV(t_2) from infl, updates to t_2 after the guard becomes true never re-trigger the constraint, silently freezing downstream flow variables below mu_S. Conversely, lazy online simplification in Mini Project 6.2 [PPA Mini Project 6.2, p. 388] (book p. 388; PDF p. 404) dynamically inserts new graph edges x_2 -> x upon guard activation, which can merge previously acyclic nodes into an SCC and invalidate static srPostorder priorities.

Guardrail: Evaluate false guards to bot_L (empty set) and register full FV(t_1) U FV(t_2) in infl (or re-enqueue and register payload on lazy activation). (Refs: F-U6-02, G-U6-05, G-U6-20).

## Summary

Length-N bit-vector W.p scans N bits per refill (O(h*N^2) under sparse refills), and Figure 6.3 row 6 displays the refilled W.c one step earlier than Table 6.3 executes (unlike Figure 6.6).

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Table 6.3, p. 376] (book p. 376; PDF p. 392)
- [PPA Figure 6.3, p. 377] (book p. 377; PDF p. 393)
- [PPA §6.2, p. 378] (book p. 378; PDF p. 394)
- [PPA Figure 6.6, p. 384] (book p. 384; PDF p. 400)
- [PPA Exercise 6.7, p. 390] (book p. 390; PDF p. 406)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 6 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

In Table 6.3 [PPA Table 6.3, p. 376] (book p. 376; PDF p. 392) and §6.2 [PPA §6.2, p. 378] (book p. 378; PDF p. 394), representing W.p as a dense length-N bit vector forces a full 1..N scan on every W.c = nil refill; on a sparse chain where each pass flips only O(1) bits across Theta(h * N) refills, scan overhead degrades to Theta(h * N^2) unless backed by a [external: sparse-set] or Exercise 6.7's two-queue routing [PPA Exercise 6.7, p. 390] (book p. 390; PDF p. 406). Independently, Figure 6.3 row 6 [PPA Figure 6.3, p. 377] (book p. 377; PDF p. 393) prints the refilled W.c one step before Table 6.3's extract() triggers the swap (whereas Figure 6.6 [PPA Figure 6.6, p. 384] (book p. 384; PDF p. 400) shows deferred refill), causing trace-oracle assertions to fail if both tables are tested against one convention.

Guardrail: Pair sparse RPO queues with [external: sparse-set] tracking or two-queue priority routing (Exercise 6.7) and document Figure 6.3's display convention. (Refs: F-U6-04, F-U6-05, G-U6-11, G-U6-12).

## Summary

Must equations (Dom, AE) require bot_L = U and join_L = intersection; Exercise 6.5 unary join splitting conflicts with universal per-update widening in Exercise 6.13 unless widening is restricted to loop-head cutsets inside the Analysis[x] not>= new guard.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Exercise 6.4, p. 389] (book p. 389; PDF p. 405)
- [PPA Exercise 6.5, p. 389] (book p. 389; PDF p. 405)
- [PPA Exercise 6.8, p. 390] (book p. 390; PDF p. 406)
- [PPA Exercise 6.13, p. 391] (book p. 391; PDF p. 407)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 6 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Three solver-composition traps arise when combining Chapter 6 exercises: (1) initialising must-analyses (Dominators in Exercise 6.4 [PPA Exercise 6.4, p. 389] (book p. 389; PDF p. 405) or Available Expressions in Exercise 6.8 [PPA Exercise 6.8, p. 390] (book p. 390; PDF p. 406)) with empty instead of bot_L = U traps the intersection join at empty permanently; (2) dropping the 'if Analysis[x] not>= new' guard before applying Analysis[x] := Analysis[x] widen new in Exercise 6.13 [PPA Exercise 6.13, p. 391] (book p. 391; PDF p. 407) can diverge or over-widen because widenings need not satisfy a widen b = a when b <= a; and (3) pairing Exercise 6.5 unary join splitting [PPA Exercise 6.5, p. 389] (book p. 389; PDF p. 405) with universal per-update widening widens acyclic branch merges (e.g., [0,0] widen [1,1] -> [0, +infty]) instead of joining them via lub.

Guardrail: Enforce explicit polarity orientation on must lattices, retain the not>= guard before widening, and aggregate acyclic joins before cutset widening. (Refs: G-U6-02, G-U6-03, G-U6-09, G-U6-10, G-U6-21, G-U6-22).

## Summary

Must equations (Dom, AE) require bot_L = U and join_L = intersection; Exercise 6.5 unary join splitting conflicts with universal per-update widening in Exercise 6.13 unless widening is restricted to loop-head cutsets inside the Analysis[x] not>= new guard.

## Source Citations & Grounding

- [PPA Exercise 6.4, p. 389] (book p. 389; PDF p. 405)
- [PPA Exercise 6.5, p. 389] (book p. 389; PDF p. 405)
- [PPA Exercise 6.8, p. 390] (book p. 390; PDF p. 406)
- [PPA Exercise 6.13, p. 391] (book p. 391; PDF p. 407)
- Statements confirmed against rendered page images during Unit 6 extraction and pre-promotion audit.

## Technical Analysis / Mechanism

Three solver-composition traps arise when combining Chapter 6 exercises: (1) initialising must-analyses (Dominators in Exercise 6.4 [PPA Exercise 6.4, p. 389] (book p. 389; PDF p. 405) or Available Expressions in Exercise 6.8 [PPA Exercise 6.8, p. 390] (book p. 390; PDF p. 406)) with empty instead of bot_L = U traps the intersection join at empty permanently; (2) dropping the 'if Analysis[x] not>= new' guard before applying Analysis[x] := Analysis[x] widen new in Exercise 6.13 [PPA Exercise 6.13, p. 391] (book p. 391; PDF p. 407) can diverge or over-widen because widenings need not satisfy a widen b = a when b <= a; and (3) pairing Exercise 6.5 unary join splitting [PPA Exercise 6.5, p. 389] (book p. 389; PDF p. 405) with universal per-update widening widens acyclic branch merges (e.g., [0,0] widen [1,1] -> [0, +infty]) instead of joining them via lub.
